answer: Polling a separate asynchronous status resource is unnecessary when the work can finish inside a single request: i.e., when a same-connection synchronous (unary) response suffices because the API responds quickly enough to return the one final result or error before the request is released. In that case the client holds one request and reads the outcome directly, so no operation handle, status endpoint, backoff/expiry policy, handle store or terminal-state schema is warranted. The Asynchronous Request-Reply pattern is only a good fit when the work does not fit a same-connection response, and it is a hard contraindication when a synchronous response suffices or duplicate submission cannot be made idempotent. Even when accepted work does outlive the request transport, a durable operation ID and status read are required, but polling is only one option for status updates — webhooks or a stream can carry them instead, so a client-side poll loop is not mandatory whenever a push channel is available.
